title: Retrospective Cost Analysis of the Treatment of Emergency Patients at an Emergency Department Followed by Transfer to External Hospitals: A Comparison Between Actual Treatment Costs and Reimbursement Received
summary: The planned study will examine whether revenue covers the actual treatment costs in the ED of a university hospital. It will include patients who were initially treated in the ED in 2025 and subsequently transferred to other hospitals for further care because of insufficient bed capacity. Anonymized data from patient records will be analyzed retrospectively. The study aims to determine the extent of any differences between costs and revenue. It will also examine which care processes, medical conditions, and reasons for transfer are associated with costs exceeding revenue. The findings are intended to help improve clinical workflows and financial planning. They will also provide a basis for health policy decisions and appropriate reimbursement for emergency care.
conditions: Patients transferred from ED to other hospitals

interventions.name: Against this backdrop, the planned retrospective health economic analysis aims to systematically compare the actual treatment costs incurred in the Emergency Department (ED) of an university hospital for the period from January 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025, with the reimbursement revenues generated

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Treatment in the ED of University Hospital Düsseldorf between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2025.

Transfer to another hospital following completion of the acute diagnostic work-up and initial treatment, including monitoring in the ED if required.

The study will retrospectively include all patients who were treated in the ED during the specified period and subsequently required transfer to another hospital.
Exclusion criteria:
•    Patients who were discharged directly as outpatients or were not transferred to an external facility.
•    Patients transferred internally within the same hospital (no external transfer).
•    Patients who died while in the ED.
•    Cases with incorrect or inconsistent data records that do not allow for the calculation of costs or revenues.
